text: In the definition of an eigenvector of a linear operator T, the vector v must satisfy:
choices: Tv = λv for some scalar λ, with v ≠ 0
Tv = λv for some scalar λ, with v allowed to be 0
explanation: Eigenvectors are required to be nonzero: since T(0) = λ·0 for every scalar λ, allowing v = 0 would make every scalar an eigenvalue. Tv = v is only the special case λ = 1.
